In [[number theory]], the '''Artin conductor''' is a number or [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] associated to a [[character theory|character]] of a [[Galois group]] of a [[local field|local]] or [[global field|global]] [[field (mathematics)|field]], introduced by [[Emil Artin]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Artin |first=Emil |author1-link=Emil Artin |title=Zur Theorie der L-Reihen mit allgemeinen Gruppencharakteren |language=de |year=1930 |journal=Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg |volume=8 |pages=292–306 |doi=10.1007/BF02941010 |jfm=56.0173.02}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Artin |first=Emil |author1-link=Emil Artin |title=Die gruppentheoretische Struktur der Diskriminanten algebraischer Zahlkörper | url=https://resolver.sub.uni-goettingen.de/purl?GDZPPN002171422 |language=de |year=1931 |journal=[[Journal für die Reine und Angewandte Mathematik]] |volume=164 |pages=1–11 |doi=10.1515/crll.1931.164.1 |zbl=0001.00801}}</ref> as an expression appearing in the [[functional equation]] of an [[Artin L-function]].

== Local Artin conductors ==

Suppose that <math>L</math> is a finite [[Galois extension]] of the local field <math>K</math>, with Galois group <math>G</math>. If <math>\chi</math> is a character of <math>G</math>, then the Artin conductor of <math>\chi</math> is the number
:<math>f(\chi)=\sum_{i\ge 0}\frac{g_i}{g_0}(\chi(1)-\chi(G_i)),</math>
where <math>G_i</math> is the <math>i</math>-th [[ramification group]] (in [[lower numbering]]), of order <math>g_i</math>, and <math>\chi(G_i)</math> is the average value of <math>\chi</math> on <math>G_i</math>.{{sfnp|Serre|1967|p=158}} The local conductor is an integer.{{sfnp|Serre|1967|p=159}}{{sfnp|Manin|Panchishkin|2005|p=329}} Heuristically, the Artin conductor measures how far the action of the higher ramification groups is from being trivial. In particular, if <math>\chi</math> is unramified, then its Artin conductor is zero. Thus, if <math>L</math> is unramified over <math>K</math>, then the Artin conductors of all <math>\chi</math> are zero.

The ''wild invariant''{{sfnp|Manin|Panchishkin|2005|p=329}} or ''Swan conductor''{{sfnp|Snaith|1994|p=249}} of the character is

:<math> f(\chi) - (\chi(1)-\chi(G_0)),  </math>

in other words, the sum of the higher order terms with <math>i>0</math>.

== Global Artin conductors ==

The '''global Artin conductor''' of a representation <math>\chi</math> of the Galois group <math>G</math> of a finite extension <math>L/K</math> of global fields is an ideal of <math>K</math>, defined to be

:<math>\mathfrak{f}(\chi) = \prod_p p^{f(\chi,p)}</math>

where the product is over the primes <math>p</math> of <math>K</math>, and <math>f(\chi,p)</math> is the local Artin conductor of the restriction of <math>\chi</math> to the decomposition group of some prime of <math>L</math> lying over <math>p</math>.{{sfnp|Serre|1967|p=159}} Since the local Artin conductor is zero at unramified primes, the above product only need be taken over primes that ramify in <math>L/K</math>.

== Artin representation and Artin character ==
{{further|Galois module#Artin representations}}

Suppose that <math>L</math> is a finite Galois extension of the local field <math>K</math>, with Galois group <math>G</math>. The '''Artin character''' <math>a_G</math> of <math>G</math> is the character

:<math>a_G=\sum_\chi f(\chi)\chi</math>

and the '''Artin representation''' <math>A_G</math> is the complex linear representation of ''G'' with this character. {{harvtxt|Weil|1946}} asked for a direct construction of the Artin representation. {{harvs|txt|last=Serre|year=1960}} showed that the Artin representation can be realized over the local field <math>\Q_\ell</math>, for any prime <math>\ell</math> not equal to the residue characteristic <math>p</math>. {{harvtxt|Fontaine|1971}} showed that it can be realized over the corresponding ring of Witt vectors. It cannot in general be realized over the rationals or over the local field <math>\Q_p</math>, suggesting that there is no easy way to construct the Artin representation explicitly.{{sfnp|Serre|1967|p=160}}

== Swan representation ==

The '''Swan character''' ''sw''<sub>''G''</sub> is given by

:<math>sw_G= a_G -r_G+1 </math>

where ''r''<sub>''g''</sub> is the character of the regular representation and 1 is the character of the trivial representation.{{sfnp|Snaith|1994|p=248}} The Swan character is the character of a representation of ''G''. {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Richard Swan|last=Swan|year=1963}} showed that there is a unique [[projective module|projective]] representation of ''G'' over the [[p-adic integer|''l''-adic integers]] with character the Swan character.

== Applications ==

The Artin conductor appears in the [[conductor-discriminant formula]] for the discriminant of a global field.{{sfnp|Serre|1967|p=160}}

The optimal level in the [[Serre modularity conjecture]] is expressed in terms of the Artin conductor.

The Artin conductor appears in the functional equation of the [[Artin L-function]].

The Artin and Swan representations are used to define the [[conductor of an elliptic curve]] or abelian variety.
